findings.title: Denial cache short-circuits the DB re-query, so stale denials persist after permissions are granted
findings.body:
Check now consults `permDenialCache` before anything else and returns `Allowed:false` on a hit, without re-querying the database. Any deny is stored for `shortCacheTTL` (30s) and never invalidated.

If a check runs before a permission exists, that user/resource pair stays denied for 30s even after the grant is written. Examples: a dashboard creator whose managed permission is written just after the first check, or an admin granting access. The 'requery permissions from DB on miss' fallback, which is the stated goal of the PR, never runs during that window.

Consider not caching denials for resources newly seen in the request, using a much shorter TTL, or invalidating denials when permissions change.

findings.title: Denial cache key is ambiguous because '_' can appear in UIDs
findings.body:
`userPermDenialCacheKey` joins userUID, action, name and parent with "_". Grafana UIDs may contain underscores, so different (name, parent) pairs can produce the same key. For example, name="a_b", parent="" and name="a", parent="b_" both end in "_a_b_". A denial for one resource can then wrongly deny another.

The key also shares the ".perm_<uid>_<action>" prefix with `userPermCacheKey` in the same underlying cache, which risks cross-type collisions that only surface as unmarshal warnings.

Use a distinct prefix (e.g. ".perm_denial_") and a separator that cannot appear in UIDs, or escape/encode the components.

findings.title: Denial-cache test does not prove the denial short-circuits evaluation
findings.body:
The test comments that it seeds an allowing permission to prove the cached permissions are not checked. It actually sets `map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}`, which `checkPermission` treats as no permission.

The store is the default empty fakeStore, so the DB fallback would also deny. The assertion therefore passes even if the denial cache were never consulted.

Seed `true` (and/or DB permissions that would allow), and assert the store was not called.
